<reason>B won the debate's decisive clash: reach. B established early that the growing share of deaths are unwitnessed, unaware users (counterfeit-pill teens, adulterated cocaine), pressed it directly in Q1 (who administers naloxone at midnight?), and demolished A's answers in Rebuttal 2 — supervised consumption sites number essentially two and are legally besieged, and the unaware teen neither carries test strips nor knows he is a drug user. A's closing sidestepped the witness objection by reframing it as consent, which B's closing surgically exposed. B also answered both pressure questions with substance (Australia heroin drought plus the east-west mortality gradient; a substitution-is-not-infinite and pill-press manufacturing mechanism), and A left the substitution mechanism and "naloxone doesn't have a longitude" points unrebutted. A's interdiction-futility case was genuinely strong — the 2019 China example was turned well, and the heroin-vs-synthetic distinction on Australia was a good closing exploit — but A never closed the hole in its own strategy's coverage of the population doing much of the dying. B's clipped opening is a real execution cost, which keeps the margin moderate rather than large.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2: answered A1 with the Australia drought and "Naloxone doesn't have a longitude. Supply does," then converted A's own reach answer into the debate's killing image — essentially two supervised consumption sites, a boy who won't walk into one, won't test his pill, and "does not know he is a drug user." A never recovered that point.</best_rebuttal>
